newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mixed in thin pre-holiday volume.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mixed in thin pre-holiday volume.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mixed in thin featureless pre-Thanksgiving trade, industry sources said.
NYMEX will be closed Thursday and Friday for the U.S. holiday, and many players were said to have taken Wednesday off as well.

As of 1200 EST, January California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down eight cents at $26.10 after trading as low as $25.70 per megawatt hour (MWh), while February COB was offered at $20.60 and bid at $20.00 per MWh.
January Palo Verde (PV) had traded up 66 cents at $25.50 but was bid at $25.70 and offered at $26.00 per MWh, while February PV was offered at $22.15 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1130 EST a total of 19 COB and five PV contracts had traded.
